class.name: VoxelTerrain3D
class.brief_description: Terrain made of voxels, with caves, overhangs and tunnels, that can be dug into while the game runs.
class.description: Where [Terrain3D] stores one height for each point on a grid, a voxel terrain stores the ground itself, as a grid of voxels that are either in the ground or in the air. That lets it have caves, arches, overhangs and tunnels, and lets a game dig into it or build onto it. The shape starts from the [VoxelGenerator] in [member data]: flat ground, hills, caves carved by noise, or the heights of an existing [TerrainData]. Only voxels that have been changed are stored, so the world can stretch as far as [member view_distance] without costing anything to save. The surface is drawn in blocks of 32 voxels. Blocks near the viewer are drawn at full detail and each step further out uses blocks twice the size at half the detail, so distant ground stays cheap. Blocks are built on worker threads, and a block keeps its old mesh until its new one is ready, so neither camera moves nor edits ever leave gaps. [signal meshing_finished] says when everything in view is up to date. Collision is built around the viewer, out to [member collision_distance], at full detail. Layers work as they do on [Terrain3D]: each voxel is made of one [TerrainLayer], and the surface blends between neighbouring voxels. Every layer is projected from all three axes, so cave ceilings and cliffs are textured as well as the ground. In the editor, select the node and use the Terrain dock to sculpt: Add, Dig, Smooth, Flatten and Paint, each with undo. A [Terrain3D] can be turned into a voxel terrain with Terrain > Convert to Voxel Terrain in the dock, which keeps its shape, layers and paint. Digging at runtime: [codeblock] # Blasts a crater where a grenade lands. func explode(at: Vector3): $VoxelTerrain3D.dig_sphere(at, 3.0) [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] Only the node's position is used; rotation and scale are ignored. Change [member VoxelTerrainData.voxel_size] to change the size of the voxels.

method.name: add_sphere
method.description: Adds a ball of ground of [param radius] metres at [param global_position]. The new ground is made of [param layer], or of whatever the voxels there were before when it is [code]-1[/code].

method.name: bake_mesh
method.description: Meshes the terrain inside [param global_box] into one [ArrayMesh], at a level of detail of [param lod] (0 for full detail), relative to the terrain's position. The box is rounded out to whole blocks, and at most 4096 blocks can be baked at once. The mesh has positions, normals and indices, with the layer weights in the four custom channels, four layers to each. Use it to export part of the terrain to other tools, or as a static mesh for something that should not change.

method.name: dig_sphere
method.description: Removes a ball of ground of [param radius] metres at [param global_position], leaving air.

method.name: flatten_sphere
method.description: Levels the ground within [param radius] metres of [param global_position] towards a flat surface at its height, by [param strength]: [code]1.0[/code] flattens it at once, less moves part of the way.

method.name: get_chunk_count
method.description: Returns the number of blocks currently drawn.

method.name: get_distance
method.description: Returns how far [param global_position] is from the surface, in metres: negative in the ground, positive in the air. Distances are exact near the surface and only an estimate further out.

method.name: get_layer
method.description: Returns the layer the surface near [param global_position] is made of.

method.name: get_normal
method.description: Returns the direction the surface faces near [param global_position].

method.name: get_surface_name
method.description: Returns [member TerrainLayer.surface_name] of the layer at [param global_position], for footstep sounds and the like.

method.name: global_to_voxel
method.description: Converts a global position into voxels, relative to the terrain's origin.

method.name: intersect_ray
method.description: Finds where a ray from [param from] along [param direction] first meets the ground within [param max_distance] metres. Returns a [Dictionary] with [code]position[/code] and [code]normal[/code], or an empty one if it hits nothing or starts in the ground. It reads the voxels directly, so it works beyond [member collision_distance] and before any collision is built.

method.name: is_meshing
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] while blocks in view are still being built. A loading screen can wait for this to become [code]false[/code], or for [signal meshing_finished].

method.name: paint_sphere
method.description: Paints the surface within [param radius] metres of [param global_position] with [param layer].

method.name: rebuild
method.description: Builds every block again. Changes to the data rebuild the blocks they touch on their own; this is for after changing something the terrain cannot see, such as a [Noise] resource the generator uses being edited through code.

method.name: smooth_sphere
method.description: Smooths the ground within [param radius] metres of [param global_position], by [param strength] from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].

method.name: voxel_to_global
method.description: Converts a position in voxels, relative to the terrain's origin, into a global position.

members.member: How far from the viewer, in metres, the terrain has collision. Blocks this close are always drawn at full detail, and their collision matches what is drawn. Physics further away than this finds no ground, so keep anything that needs it, such as enemies, within this distance of the viewer, or set [member viewer_path] to follow the player rather than the camera.
If [code]true[/code], the terrain has collision near the viewer.
The physics layers the terrain is in.
The physics layers the terrain scans. Static ground rarely needs this.
The terrain's priority in resolving collisions. See [member CollisionObject3D.collision_priority].
The voxels, generator and layers. Save it as its own file to share it between scenes; the editor does this automatically the first time the terrain is edited.
Shows the terrain in a diagnostic view instead of its layers. An editing aid; it is not saved with the scene.

How far from the viewer, in metres, the terrain is drawn at full detail. Each level of detail after that reaches twice as far as the one before. Raise it for more detail in the distance at the cost of more triangles.
The render layers the terrain is drawn on.
How the layers are blended. The same [TerrainMaterial] can be shared with [Terrain3D] nodes; its wetness settings do not apply to voxel terrain.
How far from the viewer, in metres, the terrain is drawn.
The node the terrain builds detail and collision around. When empty, the current camera is used, or in the editor, the editor's camera.

signal.name: meshing_finished
signal.description: Emitted when every block in view has been built, after the view moved or the terrain changed.

constants.constant: Shows which way the surface faces, as colour.
Shows each layer as a flat colour.
Shows each level of detail as a colour.
The terrain casts shadows from both sides of its surface.
The terrain only casts shadows and is not drawn itself.
